_meta.description: The SAFE, auto-rewritable subset of removed-functions.json: global functions removed at a major whose replacement is an exact 1:1 global-function rename with a compatible call signature for the dominant call shape. Consumed PER-MAJOR by the data-driven AST rules ElggMigrate\Rules\V2ToV3\RemovedFunctionRenames (3.x), V3ToV4\RemovedFunctionRenames (4.x), V4ToV5\RemovedFunctions (5.x), V5ToV6\RemovedFunctions (6.x) and V6ToV7\RemovedFunctions (7.x) — all via Rules\Shared\DataDrivenRemovedFunctions — which rewrite FuncCall names in place AT THE STEP WHERE THE FUNCTION ACTUALLY BREAKS. Entries whose replacement is prose, needs new arguments, changes semantics, or is a method/service call (e.g. ELGG's AMD->ESM migration, elgg_set_ignore_access -> elgg_call(...), elgg_reset_system_cache -> _elgg_services()->systemCache->clear()) are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED here — they stay LLM-guided in the manifest because a blind rename would corrupt code.
_meta.relationship: This is a strict subset of references/removed-functions.json (which drives DETECTION/flagging in PostMigrationVerifier + VersionGuard --check, cumulatively). This file drives REWRITING and is per-major. Each function's top-level block here MUST equal its removal major in removed-functions.json — a mismatch means the rename fires at the wrong migration step (the exact bug fixed under bd elgg-migrate-jfrc1). This invariant is enforced by tests/Rules/Shared/RenameMapPlacementTest.php.
_meta.signature_note: For multi-arg helpers included here (forward, register_error, system_message), the rename is correct for the dominant single-message/single-url call; the manifest's LLM instructions still cover the rarer multi-arg reason/priority cases.
_meta.placement_note: Placement reconciled 2026-07-09 (bd elgg-migrate-jfrc1) against the core-verified removed-functions.json (commit d9df460): forward / register_error / system_message / current_page_url / elgg_get_version are removed at 5.x (NOT 6.x); elgg_redirect / _elgg_rmdir / _elgg_html_decode / elgg_get_logged_in_user at 3.x; elgg_flush_caches at 4.x. Previously these all sat in the 6.x block, so a 4x->5x or 5x->6x migration never rewrote them at the step where they break. register_error -> elgg_register_error_message (NOT elgg_register_error, which does not exist).
